ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A uniform resistive wire carries a current with constant magnitude and direction. If the amount of charge passing through a cross-section of the wire in time $t=2\mathbf{s}$ is $q=1\mathrm{C}$, and the heat generated by the wire in the same time is $Q=25\mathrm{J}$.

1. What is the current $I$ through the resistance wire?
2. What is the resistance $R$ of this resistance wire?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A uniform resistive wire carries a current with constant magnitude and direction. If the amount of charge passing through a cross-section of the wire in time $t=2\mathbf{s}$ is $q=1\mathrm{C}$, and the heat generated by the wire in the same time is $Q=25\mathrm{J}$. 1. What is the current $I$ through the resistance wire? 2. What is the resistance $R$ of this resistance wire?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given q = 1 C, t = 2 s, and heat Q = 25 J. The current is constant, so I = q/t = 1 C / 2 s = 0.5 A. Joule heating is Q = I^2 R t. Rearranging gives R = Q/(I^2 t). Substituting I = 0.5 A and t = 2 s: R = 25 / ((0.5)^2 * 2) = 25 / (0.25 * 2) = 25 / 0.5 = 50 ohms.
